subject: RE: Request for VM evidence and SLA cadence (Acme Financial)
messages:
From: Laura Simmons <laura.simmons@acme-fin.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: security@acme-fin.com, Connor Blake <connor.blake@acme-fin.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request for VM evidence and SLA cadence (Acme Financial)

Diego,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our SOC 2 readiness and the SIG review, the audit team has asked for a concise vulnerability management evidence packet that includes:

- Weekly vulnerability scan cadence history for the last 90 days (scan tool, scope, and sample scan index)
- SLA windows for CVE remediation by severity (Critical / High / Medium / Low)
- Owner assignments and escalation flow for exceptions
- A written attestation for recent remediations of three critical CVEs we flagged in March (tracker IDs attached below)

Can you assemble a single packet (PDF) we can drop into the SIG portal by next Tuesday? If possible include a short narrative describing how prefix/KV cache and deployment rollouts reduce blast radius for config-related patches (our auditors asked about patch impact mitigation).

Appreciate a short call if needed — we can do 30 minutes Monday.

Best,

Laura Simmons
Director, Risk and Compliance
Acme Financial

Attachments: ACME-Tracker-IDs.csv (referenced)

From: diego.fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Simmons <laura.simmons@acme-fin.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request for VM evidence and SLA cadence (Acme Financial)

Laura —

Thanks for the clear ask. We can produce a consolidated packet and will include:

1) Scan index (90-day window) with sample scan XML and exported CSV rows — summarized in a 2-page index (acme_vm_scan_index_202704.pdf).
2) SLA matrix for CVE remediation by severity with our on-call escalation (redwood_cve_sla_matrix_202705.pdf).
3) Formal attestation letter for the three March critical CVEs, including commit hashes and patch timestamps (cve-closure-commitment_acme-202705.pdf).
4) Short narrative on how we mitigate patch blast radius via staged canary rollouts, model pinning, and KV cache isolation for inference services.

Quick notes on cadence and SLAs (summary):
- Critical: 24 hours to mitigation w/ hotfix or temporary mitigations and continuous monitoring until full patch deployed.
- High: 72 hours to confirmed mitigation plan and prioritized patch within 7 days.
- Medium: 14-day window to remediation planning and deployment within 30 days.
- Low: tracked and remediated per release cycle (60–90 days).

Kimberly (cc) will attach the formal remediation attestation text and the commit/rollback log excerpt. Marissa will upload the packet to a shared Drive and drop the HubSpot record link once ready.

We can aim to have the packet to you by Monday EOD PST so you have time before Tuesday's SIG upload. If you want the Monday call, I can do 10–11am PST.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Security Programs Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments (sent with follow-ups): acme_vm_scan_index_202704.pdf (summary), redwood_cve_sla_matrix_202705.pdf

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: Laura Simmons <laura.simmons@acme-fin.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request for VM evidence and SLA cadence (Acme Financial)

Diego / Laura —

Attestation (formal text below) prepared for inclusion in the packet: please use as the signed statement on company letterhead. I will also add the commit hashes and verification timestamps in the appendix.

-----
Redwood Inference 
Vulnerability Remediation Attestation

This letter attests that Redwood Inference identified and remediated the following CVEs referenced in ACME tracker IDs (March 2027): CVE-2027-1987 (Critical), CVE-2027-2034 (Critical), CVE-2027-2145 (High). Remediation actions were completed and validated as follows:

- CVE-2027-1987: Hotfix deployed to dedicated inference pool on 2027-03-19T02:18:00Z; verification scans completed 2027-03-19T06:42:00Z. Commit: a1f3c8d.
- CVE-2027-2034: Temporary mitigation (config isolation) applied 2027-03-20T05:00:00Z; full patch deployed 2027-03-22T22:37:00Z. Commit: b4d0e5f.
- CVE-2027-2145: Priority patching completed 2027-03-25T11:12:00Z; post-deploy scan clear 2027-03-25T14:20:00Z. Commit: c7e9a11.

All remediation activities were performed under our change control process with rollback plans and verification scans. Exceptions and the corresponding mitigation logs are available in the appendix (JIRA: SECOPS-4123).

Signed,
Kimberly Park
Director, Vulnerability Management
Redwood Inference
-----

SLA clarifications (technical): for critical hotfixes we apply continuous scan/telemetry monitoring for 72 hours post-deploy and elevate to incident commander if regression signals exceed threshold.

I will upload appendix extracts to the drive folder and attach the single-page attestation PDF.

—Kimberly

Attachment: cve-closure-commitment_acme-202705.pdf

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Packet uploaded to Drive and shared with your security@acme-fin.com address: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AqR-ACME-VM-PACK

Files included: acme_vm_scan_index_202704.pdf, redwood_cve_sla_matrix_202705.pdf, cve-closure-commitment_acme-202705.pdf, appendix_scan_export_202704.zip (scan CSV snippets), and a short README.md that maps each item to SIG/CAIQ control IDs.

I've also created a HubSpot attachment on your account for traceability: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/ACME-FIN-9876. If you'd like a signed DocuSign for the attestation letter, say the word and we'll route it.

Marissa Cole

Diego / Kimberly / Marissa —

Received, and thank you — this is exactly what the audit team needed. I reviewed the attestation and the SLA matrix quickly; the timeline entries for the March fixes map cleanly to our tracker IDs. We'll upload the packet to SIG tonight.

Two quick asks: 1) can you include the one-line verification command we used (scan tool invocation) in the README so auditors can reproduce the check, and 2) please send a signed DocuSign for the attestation letter (we need signatures on letterhead).

Laura
